title: RedTrack tells customers an attacker reached its log store, which held API keys, ad-network tokens and certificate private keys
date_note: Notice to customers sent 24 November (the day Privacy Affairs published); the article places the attack on 22 and 23 November.
geo_basis: country stated by the source (RedTrack Technologies Ltd, Cyprus); no city stated
summary: Privacy Affairs, citing a notice RedTrack sent customers on 24 November, reports an attacker reached the ad tracker's log store, which held API keys, session tokens, ad-network tokens and private keys of customer certificates. RedTrack says its logs show no access to the click, conversion and report databases. It says misuse was found in 3 advertising accounts and phishing or fraud was tied to 7 accounts.
plain: Ad-tracking company RedTrack says an attacker got into logs containing customers' keys and tokens. RedTrack says it replaced all user, publisher and advertiser API keys.
exec: RedTrack told customers that keys and tokens stored in its logs were reachable by an attacker, so linked ad accounts may need new credentials, according to Privacy Affairs.
action: Per RedTrack's notice as relayed by Privacy Affairs: update API keys in all integrations, renew stored ad-network credentials, and have the CA revoke any certificate you uploaded.

validation.note: Only Privacy Affairs read; it relays RedTrack's customer notice (the notice itself and RedTrack's website were not read).
